This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.

2. The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 18.07.2022 at about 6.30 p.m. he had been riding his motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-43-R-7613 at SCCH-5 Sulibele Road, near Raini Farm,
Devanahalli, Bengaluru District, at that time, a Penna Cement Lorry bearing Reg.
No.KA-01-AF-6856 being driven by its driver at high speed and hit front portion of his bike.
Due to the said impact, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Immediately after the accident, he was taken to Sri Shirdi Sai Hospital, Devanahalli, wherein he took treatment as inpatient.

3. At the time of accident, he was hale and healthy, aged about 27 years, working as Security in hotel,
thereby earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
Due to the injuries sustained in the alleged accident, he was unable to work and earn his livelihood.

The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending Penna Cement Lorry by its driver and Devanahalli Traffic Police have registered a case in crime SCCH-5 No.95/2022 for the offences punishable under Sec.279 and 337 of IPC.

The 1st Respondent being the R.C.Owner and 2nd Respondent being the insurer of the offending lorry,
they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- to the petitioner with interest.
4. In pursuance of service of notice, the Respondent No.1/owner has appeared before the tribunal through his counsel and filed written statement and denied averments of the petition.

He has admitted that he is R.C.Owner of the lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-01-AF-6856 and the said vehicle is having valid insurance with respondent No.2 vide policy No.61070031220100000545 which is valid from 19.05.2022 to 18.05.2023 and there is no negligence on the part of driver of the said vehicle who is having valid driving licence as on the date of SCCH-5 accident.

Further denied age,
occupation and income of the petitioner.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
5. Respondent No.2/insurer has appeared before the tribunal through counsel and filed written statement by denying entire averments of the petition.

Further admitted issuance of insurance policy bearing No.61070031220100000545 valid from 19.05.2022 to 18.05.2023 in respect of Penna Cement Lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-01-AF-6856 and if there is any liability to pay the compensation

,
it is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further the driver of the said lorry did not possessed valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.

He has denied age,
occupation, income of the petitioner, injuries sustained by him and treatment taken by him.

Further submitted that, accident took place on 18.07.2022, but FIR has filed on 19.07.2022 by SCCH-5 which petitioner colluding with respondent No.1 and jurisdictional police has filed police complaint against him.
Compensation claimed by the petitioner is on higher side.

Accordingly prays to dismiss Babu Reddy.N vs Poineer Builders Ltd on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192992340/

6. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1. Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 18.07.2022 at about 6.30 p.m. when petitioner was riding his motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-43-R-7613 near Sulibele Road, Rajini Farm, Devanahalli, Bengaluru, at that time, Penna Cement Lorry bearing Reg.
No.KA-01-AF-6856 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the petitioner, as mentioned in claim petition?
2.
Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so how much and from whom?
SCCH-5 3. What order or award?

7. In order to prove his case, petitioner himself deposed his evidence as PW-1, examined Record Manager at Sri Shirdi Sai Hospital as PW-2, Dr.S.A.Somashekara, Orthopaedic Surgeon at Bowring & Lady Curzon Hospital as PW-3 and marked 20 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.20 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, respondent No.2 has not lead any evidence.

8. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:
SCCH-5 ::REASONS::
9. Issue No.1:- The petitioner inorder to prove her case, he himself examined as PW-1 and in his chief- examination evidence, he has reiterated petition averments.
Though he has been elaborately cross- examined by the Respondent No.2 counsel, but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the evidence of the petitioner.

10. Further to substantiate his case, petitioner has examined Record Manager/Administrator at Sri Shirdi Sai Hospital as PW-2, Dr.S.A.Somashekara Orthopaedic Surgeon at Bowring & Lady Curzon Hospital as PW-2, who examined the petitioner has stated that, petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.

Apart from the oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked copy of FIR marked as Ex.P.1, copy of SCCH-5 complaint marked as Ex.P.2, copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of spot mahazar is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of sketch is marked as Ex.P.6, copy of Sec.133 notice is marked as Ex.P.7, copy of reply notice is marked as Ex.P.8.
12.

Per contra, except appearance, filing of written statement, respondents have not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioner about causing of the injuries to the petitioner out of the accident held on 18.07.2022 at about 6.30 p.m. when he was riding his motor cycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-43-R-7613 on Sulibele Road, near Rajini Farm, Devanahalli, SCCH-5 Bengaluru District.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioner.
13. On the other hand, there is no defence evidence and the police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the driver of the offending lorry.

Under such circumstances,
considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioner, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the above issue No.1 in his favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
14. Issue No.2:-

As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained crush injury of right foot with open fracture 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th metatarsals, for which he underwent surgery in the form of wound SCCH-5 debridement + K-wire fixation for 2 nd, 3rd and 4th metatarsals.

In this regard, he has exhibited copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.7, discharge summary marked as Ex.P.9,
discharge summary marked as Ex.P.10 issued by Sri Shirdi Sai Hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient from 18.07.2022 to 22.07.2022.

Further he has furnished medial bills to the tune of Rs.1,09,936/- marked as Ex.P.12, medical prescriptions marked as Ex.P.13, CT-Scan films marked as Ex.P.14, X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.15, photos with CD marked as Ex.P.16.
15.

In order to prove his case, he has examined Record Manager/Administrator at Sri Shirdi Sai Hospital by name Girish as PW-2, who has furnished authorization letter marked as Ex.P.17, IP records SCCH-5 marked as Ex.P.18, copy of MLC Register marked as Ex.P.19 and copy of police intimation marked as Ex.P.20.
16.

Further Dr.S.A.Somashekara, Orthopaedic Surgeon at Bowring & Lady Curzon Hospital is examined as PW-3 and exhibited OPD Card marked as Ex.P.19 and X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.20.
In his affidavit evidence he has deposed that, the total disability of the petitioner of right lower limb at 34% and that of his whole body disability is 17%.

17. In cross-examination PW-3 has categorically admitted that, he has not treated the petitioner,
after 15 months from the date of accident, he has seen the petitioner for the first time and he has seen wound certificate and discharge summary.
Further deposed that, fractures are united, out of 4 fractures, 2 fractures are mal united.

Under such circumstances, considering the SCCH-5 nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and also by relying on citation reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343 Babu Reddy.N vs Poineer Builders Ltd on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192992340/
4 between Rajkumar V/s. Ajay Kumar, the functional disability of the petitioner is considered at the rate of 11% i.e., 1/3rd to the whole body out of 34% of right lower limb, for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

21. Further admittedly petitioner has exhibited Ex.P.12 medical bills for Rs.1,09,936/-.
On perusal of the said bills it is clearly stated about spending of amount for this treatment is considered.

Further on perusal of SCCH-5 Ex.P.9 in which Doctor who have treated has categorically stated that,
petitioner has sustained grievous injuries out of the accident caused on 18.07.2022.

So as per Ex.P.9 wound certificate, petitioner has sustained laceration over right parieto- temporal region, fracture metatarsal right foot, crush injury to right foot and open fracture of 2 nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th metatarsal, which are grievous in nature.
Further the Investigation Officer has also filed charge sheet against Naveen Kumar T.S. for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC.

So the said charge sheet materials and evidence of PW-1 to PW-3 clearly states that, petitioner is suffering from grievous injury out of the accident caused in the alleged accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for medical expenses of Rs.1,09,936/-.

Considering the nature of the injuries, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.15,000/-
towards pain and sufferings.
The Petitioner was treated as inpatient for a period of 4 days at Sri Shirdi Sai Hospital.
Considering the duration of treatment, a sum of Rs.15,000/- is awarded towards conveyance, nourishment and attendant charges.

Considering the injuries sustained by the petitioner and disability as stated by the Doctor and on account of the discomfort and unhappiness the claimant has to undergo in his future life, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.15,000/-
towards loss of amenities.

23. Per contra except denial in the written statement and oral evidence, respondents have not taken any endeavors to step into witness box nor to prove the allegations as alleged in the written statement.

In the SCCH-5 absence of rebuttal evidence, merely respondents have filed written statement and they have denied entire case of the petitioner are all not sufficient to disbelieve the petitioner case, because it is bounden duty of them to prove the defence as taken in the written statement.
24. Accordingly, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-
Sl.No .
Head of Compensation Amount in Rs.
1. Loss of Future Income 3,30,990-00 2.
Pain and
sufferings 15,000-00
3. Conveyance, nourishment and 15,000-00 attendant charges 4.
Medical Expenses 1,09,936-00 5. Loss of amenities in life 15,000-00 6. Loss of income during laid up 1,967-00 period Total 4,87,893-00 25.

Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.4,87,893/- with SCCH-5 interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.
26. Though the Respondents have taken several defence in their respective written statement, but whatever defence taken by them is not at all established except by leading evidence.

In other words,
the respondents have not lead any evidence to disprove the case of the petitioner.

The Respondent No.2 in its written statement admits that, it has issued policy with respect to lorry bearing Reg.
No.KA-01-AF-6856 vide its policy No.610700312201000005433 valid from 19.05.2022 to 18.05.2023, the alleged accident was occurred on 18.07.2022.

Therefore, as on the date of accident,
the insurance policy of the offending vehicle was valid and is in force.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the R.C.Owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the SCCH-5 offending lorry car Babu Reddy.N vs Poineer Builders Ltd on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192992340/
6 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.

However, as discussed above,
the insurance policy of the offending vehicle was valid and is in force as on the date of accident.
hence the respondent No.2 Insurance Company shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
Accordingly I answer Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.

27. Issue No.3: For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,87,893/- (Rupees Four Lakhs Eighty Seven Thousand Eight Hundred Ninety Three Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
SCCH-5 The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
